cards.subject: A brand
says: is one company or project
owns its own channels, media, calendar, team and timezone
is the central table that channels and posts belong to
cards.use: need to know which unit owns the channels, team and timezone
not: is a single account on a single platform

cards.subject: A channel
says: is a single account on a single platform
is owned by one brand
is either manual or live in mode
cards.use: need the unit that stands for one account on one platform
not: is shared across every brand in the app

cards.subject: The composer
says: lets you write base copy once and override it per channel
shows live character counts while you type
applies the rules of each platform to the post
cards.use: need to write one idea and tune it for each platform
not: publishes the post without any approval step

cards.subject: The calendar
says: shows every brand on one month grid
colour-codes the brands
lets you drag a post to move it
cards.use: want to see every brand's posts on one month grid
not: shows only the posts of the brand you are signed in to first

cards.subject: The publish queue
says: holds anything due on a manual channel
gives copy buttons, the media to download and platform-specific steps
marks a post published once you tick it off
cards.use: need to post by hand on a platform that has no write API
not: lists only posts that have already failed

cards.subject: Analytics
says: shows what went out and where
shows whatever metrics the platform returns
cards.use: want to see what was published and the metrics the platform handed back
not: invents reach figures for platforms that report none

cards.subject: The playbook
says: holds the master instructions for every format and every kind of engagement work
has limits the app checks by itself, such as hashtag count and copy length
lets each brand follow the master and tune any limit
cards.use: need the written rule that a post or reply must follow
not: is edited only through a server deploy

cards.subject: A manual channel
says: is useful immediately without platform credentials
queues the post in the publish queue at the right time
ends with a person clicking publish
gets the same composer validation, calendar slot and approval flow as a live channel
cards.use: have a platform with no write API for organic content
not: is a stub that skips validation and approval

cards.subject: A live channel
says: publishes by itself through the platform API
needs credentials from the platform before it works
cards.use: want the app to publish without a person clicking anything
not: skips the composer's per-platform validation

cards.subject: Base copy
says: is written once for a post
can be overridden for an individual channel
is the starting text that each post target inherits
cards.use: write the same idea for several channels and then tune a few of them
not: is locked once a post has more than one target

cards.subject: A post target
says: exists once per channel on a post
has its own status separate from the post's status
may override the base copy
cards.use: need the part of a post that belongs to one channel
not: is the same record as the post itself

cards.subject: The channel catalogue
says: covers 109 platforms in 11 categories
has 45 live platforms and 64 manual-only platforms
is searchable and grouped by category
cards.use: are asked how many platforms the app covers
not: has more live platforms than manual-only ones

cards.subject: The activity checklist
says: catches up with the work that actually happened every hour
takes its counts from facts such as posts published and comments answered
never overwrites a check that a person recorded
cards.use: ask what keeps the checklist up to date without manual ticking
not: is filled in only by the performance analyst once a month

cards.subject: A tracked short link
says: uses a random 7-character code
returns nothing but a 302 to the link's destination
is followed by strangers, so it has to get past the basic-auth wall
cards.use: are asked how /l/ links behave
not: shows a 401 password prompt to every reader by design

cards.subject: The Reddit rule
says: requires both a title and a subreddit
treats a missing subreddit as an invalid post
cards.use: post to Reddit and need to know what the composer demands
not: needs only media

cards.subject: The YouTube rule
says: requires a title
is one of the per-platform rules that the composer checks
cards.use: are about to compose a YouTube post and need to know what it requires
not: requires a subreddit

cards.subject: The Instagram rule
says: requires media
stops a text-only post from passing validation
cards.use: post to Instagram and the composer complains about the post
not: requires a title and a subreddit

cards.subject: The X length cap
says: limits a post to 280 characters
is checked against the live character count
cards.use: need the number a post to X must stay under
not: is 500 characters

cards.subject: X threading
says: splits a long post into a thread on blank lines
lets one composer text become several connected posts
cards.use: want a long text on X to become a thread
not: splits on every full stop

cards.subject: A per-channel override
says: replaces the base copy for one channel only
leaves the other channels' copy unchanged
cards.use: need one channel to say something different from the base copy
not: changes the copy for every channel of the brand

cards.subject: A playbook must
says: is a rule that scheduling and approval refuse to let a post break
is checked by the composer as you type
is a safety stop for an agent run when it is broken
cards.use: learn why a post cannot be scheduled or approved even though the copy reads well
not: is only advice that can be ignored at scheduling

cards.subject: The draft status
says: is the first post status in the approval flow
comes before the post needs approval
cards.use: need the state of a post nobody has sent for review yet
not: is a target status

cards.subject: The in_review status
says: is the database status behind a post that needs approval
follows draft in the flow
cards.use: need the state of a post waiting for a sign-off
not: means the post has been published

cards.subject: The changes_requested status
says: is a post status, not a target status
records that a reviewer asked for changes instead of signing off
cards.use: are asked which post status exists because approvers can send work back
not: is a target status

cards.subject: The approved status
says: comes after in_review in the approval flow
is followed by scheduled
cards.use: need the state after sign-off and before the post is scheduled
not: comes straight after draft

cards.subject: The partially_published status
says: is a post status, separate from the target statuses
is listed after published and before failed among the post statuses
cards.use: are asked which post statuses exist besides published and failed
not: is a target status

cards.subject: The awaiting_manual status
says: is a target status, not a post status
is one of the seven target statuses
cards.use: are asked which target status is not a post status
not: is a post status

cards.subject: The post status list
says: has nine values
runs draft, in_review, changes_requested, approved, scheduled, publishing, published, partially_published and failed
cards.use: are asked how many statuses a post can have
not: has seven values

cards.subject: The target status list
says: has seven values
runs pending, scheduled, publishing, awaiting_manual, published, failed and skipped
cards.use: are asked how many statuses a post target can have
not: has nine values

cards.subject: The scheduled time
says: is stored as an absolute instant
is rendered in the brand's timezone
cards.use: need to know how a scheduled time is stored for a brand in another timezone
not: is stored as text in the brand's local time without an offset

cards.subject: The owner role
says: can do everything in the brand
can archive the brand
is the role that can switch off a workflow step's review
cards.use: need the role allowed to archive a brand
not: is read-only

cards.subject: The admin role
says: manages channels, team and content
is the minimum role for managing channels, team and the brand
cards.use: need the lowest role that can manage the team of a brand
not: can archive the brand

cards.subject: The editor role
says: can write, schedule and publish
is the minimum role for editing and publishing
cards.use: need the lowest role that can write and schedule posts
not: can manage the team

cards.subject: The approver role
says: is for review only and cannot edit
can sign off a post
cards.use: need someone who signs off content without being able to change it
not: can write and publish posts

cards.subject: The viewer role
says: is read-only
is the lowest-ranked brand role
cards.use: need to give someone access to look but not change anything
not: can approve posts

cards.subject: A brand role
says: applies to one brand only
lets one person be an editor on one company and a viewer on another
cards.use: need to explain why roles are not global
not: is set once for a user across every brand

cards.subject: The role ranking
says: orders the roles viewer, approver, editor, admin, owner
is used by a helper that checks a role is at least a minimum
cards.use: need to know how the code compares one role with another
not: ranks approver above editor

cards.subject: requireBrandRole
says: throws an error when the user lacks the needed role on that brand
is the check that server actions rely on instead of the UI
cards.use: need the check that refuses a call from a user without the role
not: hides the button in the interface

cards.subject: The super admin flag
says: is the is_super_admin column on users
defaults to false
covers a few global tasks such as editing the master playbook
cards.use: need the flag that is not a brand role
not: grants owner on every brand

cards.subject: A membership
says: links one user to one brand with a role
has a unique index so a user has at most one membership per brand
cascades on delete from users and brands
cards.use: need the table that gives a user a role on a brand
not: holds the user's password hash

cards.subject: The approving permission
says: is allowed for the approver role and for admin and above
does not include the editor role
cards.use: are told an editor wants to approve their own post and must say whether the code allows it
not: is allowed for every role at or above editor

cards.subject: Password hashing
says: uses bcrypt through bcryptjs
runs at cost 12
cards.use: are asked how passwords are stored
not: encrypts the password so it can be decrypted with APP_SECRET

cards.subject: The session token
says: is a signed JWT using HS256 through the jose library
is stored in a cookie named ggs_session
cards.use: need to know what a sign-in creates
not: is a random id stored as a database row

cards.subject: The session cookie flags
says: are httpOnly and SameSite lax
are secure in production
cards.use: need the cookie attributes of ggs_session
not: leave the cookie readable by page scripts

cards.subject: The session lifetime
says: is 30 days
is how long the ggs_session cookie stays valid
cards.use: are asked how long a signed-in session lasts
not: is one hour

cards.subject: APP_SECRET
says: signs the session tokens
encrypts the stored platform tokens
must be set to 32 or more random characters
logs everyone out and invalidates saved credentials when it changes
cards.use: need the one value whose loss logs everyone out and breaks every connected channel
not: can be rotated safely without any side effects

cards.subject: An invite
says: is looked up by token
counts only while it has not been accepted
can be tied to a sign-up link
cards.use: are asked how a sign-up link can bring a person into a brand
not: can be accepted any number of times

cards.subject: A stored platform token
says: is encrypted with APP_SECRET before it is stored
is never sent back to the browser
cards.use: need to explain what happens to a token pasted into Connect
not: is stored in plain text so it can be shown again

cards.subject: An agent API token
says: is sent in the X-Agent-Token header
starts with ggs_
is issued from Activities, AI agents
is rejected by the agent API when it is invalid or revoked
cards.use: need to call /api/agent/activities from a script
not: is sent in the Authorization header

cards.subject: The basic-auth wall
says: uses /etc/apache2/ggsocial.htpasswd
occupies the Authorization header
has to be let past for short links, media files and the agent API
cards.use: learn why the agent token travels in a different header
not: is enforced by the Next.js middleware

cards.subject: The content strategist
says: keeps the content plan ahead of the calendar
proposes new ideas from the brand book, goals and the lessons of past posts
cards.use: need the agent that proposes ideas when the plan would not cover the next weeks
not: books posts into open calendar slots

cards.subject: The content writer
says: keeps the calendar full from the plan
books each post into an open slot
revises anything a reviewer sends back using their note
cards.use: need the agent that turns planned ideas into scheduled posts
not: reads yesterday's posts every morning

cards.subject: The community manager
says: drafts replies to new comments, messages, mentions and reviews
sets tone and priority
flags anything a person must decide
cards.use: need the agent that answers audience comments and messages
not: writes the monthly report

cards.subject: The performance analyst
says: reads yesterday's posts every morning
writes the weekly review and the monthly report
cards.use: need the agent that reports on how posts performed
not: drafts replies to reviews

cards.subject: The reviewer
says: is Claude Haiku by default
scores everything an agent makes out of 100
flags risks
sends weak but safe work back once with its fixes
cards.use: need the model that checks agent output before a person is asked
not: is a human on the team with the approver role

cards.subject: The Review inbox
says: is where everything waiting on a person lands
lets you approve, send back with a note or stop the run
cards.use: need the one place for reviews, safety stops and manual steps
not: is the same screen as the publish queue

cards.subject: A workflow
says: is a set of steps done by an agent, a tool or a person
is how each kind of work is run
cards.use: need to explain how agent work is organised into steps
not: is a single Claude call

cards.subject: The publish a planned post workflow
says: is the workflow the content writer hands each post to
is one of the first three workflows
cards.use: need the workflow that takes a planned post through to publishing
not: sends replies to comments
like: The answer a comment or message workflow

cards.subject: The answer a comment or message workflow
says: sends replies through the platform on connected Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, Bluesky and Mastodon channels
carries the community manager's drafts
cards.use: need the workflow whose output is a reply to an audience member
not: plans new content ideas

cards.subject: The plan new ideas workflow
says: is the workflow that produces new ideas for the plan
is run by the content strategist
cards.use: need the workflow that keeps the plan supplied with ideas
not: publishes a post
like: The answer a comment or message workflow

cards.subject: Step review
says: is on for every step until the brand's owner switches it off
needs a reason, which is kept in the log, when it is switched off
cards.use: are asked who can stop a step from pausing for a person
not: is off for every step by default

cards.subject: A safety stop
says: pauses a run whatever the review setting
sends the item to the Review inbox
cards.use: learn why a run paused although the brand owner switched review off
not: can be disabled per brand by the owner

cards.subject: A flagged risk
says: is a risk the reviewer flags such as prices, refunds, legal or health matters
also covers an apology, a complaint, a sensitive topic or a claim it cannot check
cards.use: see a reply that mentions a refund pause for a person
not: is raised only for posts containing profanity

cards.subject: A score under the pass mark
says: is a safety stop based on the reviewer's score out of 100
uses the brand's own pass mark
cards.use: see a draft pause because the reviewer scored it low
not: uses one pass mark set globally for every brand

cards.subject: A broken playbook must
says: stops an agent run just as it stops scheduling and approval
is checked against the rule the activity follows
cards.use: see an agent's post paused for breaking a hard limit
not: is overridden when review is off

cards.subject: The reviewer being unable to run
says: is itself a safety stop
pauses work for a person instead of letting it through unchecked
cards.use: ask what happens when the reviewing model is unavailable
not: lets agent work through unchecked

cards.subject: The daily AI budget
says: is a per-brand limit that stops agent work when spent
shows today's spend on the Workflows page
cards.use: see runs pause because the brand has used up its AI allowance
not: is one global limit shared by every brand

cards.subject: A step that keeps failing
says: is a safety stop that applies to a repeatedly failing step
pauses the run whatever the review setting
cards.use: see a run stop after the same step failed again and again
not: is retried indefinitely until it succeeds

cards.subject: A failure alert
says: is emailed to each brand's owners and admins
needs RESEND_API_KEY and ALERT_FROM
is sent at most once every 12 hours
cards.use: need to know who is told when a post runs out of retries or a channel needs reconnecting
not: is sent to every member of the brand

cards.subject: DATABASE_URL
says: is the Postgres connection string
is one of the two values to fill in first in .env.local
cards.use: need the variable that points the app at its database
not: selects the media storage driver

cards.subject: CRON_SECRET
says: is the bearer token the /api/cron/publish endpoint requires
is sent as Authorization: Bearer by Vercel's cron
cards.use: need the value that protects the publish tick endpoint
not: signs the session cookie

cards.subject: APP_URL
says: is the public base URL of the app
must be reachable from the internet in production because platform APIs fetch media from it
is the base of OAuth redirect URIs
cards.use: see Instagram fail to fetch a post's media in production
not: is only used for the page title

cards.subject: MEDIA_DRIVER
says: is either local or s3
defaults to local, which writes to .data/uploads
cards.use: need to choose where uploaded media is stored
not: selects the database driver

cards.subject: The Canva variables
says: are CANVA_CLIENT_ID and CANVA_CLIENT_SECRET
enable importing Canva designs into Media
cards.use: need to turn on the Canva import button
not: enable Google Photos import

cards.subject: The Google variables
says: are GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
enable Google Photos import and Connect with Google for YouTube
cards.use: need to turn on Google Photos import and YouTube connection
not: enable Facebook sign-in

cards.subject: The Meta variables
says: are META_APP_ID and META_APP_SECRET
enable Connect with Facebook for Facebook Page and Instagram channels
cards.use: need to turn on Connect with Facebook
not: enable YouTube connection

cards.subject: RESEARCH_SIGNALS
says: can be set to off to stop the content strategist reading outside signals
makes the strategist search Hacker News for the last 30 days by default
sends only the pillar words out of the server
cards.use: are asked how to stop the strategist searching outside the app
not: reads Reddit and Google News by default

cards.subject: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
says: is optional
enables drafting with Claude and the brand agents
cards.use: need the variable without which the agents cannot run
not: is required before the app starts

cards.subject: The Claude model variables
says: are CLAUDE_WRITING_MODEL, CLAUDE_ANALYSIS_MODEL and CLAUDE_REVIEW_MODEL
default to claude-sonnet-5 for writing and analysis and claude-haiku-4-5 for review
cards.use: want to change which model writes, analyses or reviews
not: default the reviewer to the same model as the writer

cards.subject: NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY
says: is pinned in .env the first time the deploy runs
keeps unchanged server actions working across builds
is found in the /root/ggsocial-backups/env-* copies if lost
cards.use: need the key whose loss is as bad as losing APP_SECRET for open tabs
not: is stored in the git repository

cards.subject: npm run deploy
says: type-checks, lints and runs tests on your machine first
stops at the first failing step
rsyncs the tree and streams scripts/deploy-remote.sh to the server
cards.use: need the command that ships the app to the live server
not: builds directly on the production database host with no checks

cards.subject: SKIP_TESTS=1
says: skips the type-check, lint and tests in the deploy
is meant for an emergency fix
cards.use: need to ship a hotfix while the checks are failing
not: skips only the tests

cards.subject: The deploy backup step
says: backs up the database to /root/ggsocial-backups/ before anything changes
runs on the server half of the deploy
cards.use: need to know what protects the data if a schema push goes wrong
not: copies the uploads directory to S3

cards.subject: The schema push
says: runs drizzle-kit push before the restart
is run without --force so a drift that would drop data stops instead of auto-approving
cards.use: need to know why the schema is pushed before pm2 restarts
not: runs after the restart

cards.subject: The build into .next-new
says: lets the old build keep serving while the new one is built
is stamped with a deployment id
is swapped in, so only the restart is a gap
cards.use: need to explain why a failed build no longer takes the site down
not: builds in place over .next

cards.subject: The rsync --delete trap
says: deletes the production .env because it is not in the repo
is avoided with --exclude .env
also removes .env.local, which is a symlink to .env
cards.use: worry that a sync could wipe the secrets on the server
not: only deletes .next

cards.subject: The Tailwind binary trap
says: is the missing @tailwindcss/oxide-linux-x64-gnu module after npm ci
is solved by installing it with --no-save at the version of the installed oxide package
cards.use: see Cannot find module './tailwindcss-oxide.linux-x64-gnu.node' during the build
not: is solved by committing the Linux binary to the lockfile

cards.subject: The Node version trap
says: comes from bash -lc sourcing nvm and putting Node 18 first on the PATH
is avoided by putting /usr/bin first so install, build and runtime use Node 20
can leave a running server without its build directory when the build fails after rm -rf .next
cards.use: see Node.js version >=20.9.0 is required during a deploy
not: is caused by pm2 running an old Node

cards.subject: The stale tab trap
says: breaks a tab left open across a deploy with Failed to find Server Action
is fixed by a deploymentId that makes Next reload the page
needs both sides of a deploy to carry an id before it protects
cards.use: have users report errors on their next click after a deploy
not: is fixed by restarting the database

cards.subject: The live :443 vhost trap
says: is a regular file in sites-enabled, not a symlink
is the copy Apache serves, so edits to sites-available change nothing
is checked with apachectl -S
cards.use: edit the SSL vhost and see no change after a clean reload
not: is a symlink to sites-available

cards.subject: The Vercel deployment
says: needs MEDIA_DRIVER=s3 because serverless filesystems are wiped between invocations
uses vercel.json to call /api/cron/publish every five minutes
needs npm run db:push once against the production database
cards.use: are asked how to deploy to Vercel with hosted Postgres
not: works with MEDIA_DRIVER=local

cards.subject: The pm2 web process
says: is called ggsocial-web
runs next start -p 3200 on 127.0.0.1 only
cards.use: need the pm2 process that serves the site behind Apache
not: listens on a public port directly

cards.subject: The pm2 scheduler
says: is called ggsocial-scheduler
ticks /api/cron/publish every 60 seconds
calls /api/cron/agents every 5 minutes and the goals, pages and playbook endpoints hourly
cards.use: need the process that dispatches scheduled posts
not: runs inside the web process

cards.subject: The production database
says: runs in Docker as ggsocial-pg using postgres:16
keeps data in the ggsocial-pgdata volume
cards.use: need to find the production Postgres
not: is a hosted database service

cards.subject: Connect with Facebook
says: publishes to Facebook Pages and Instagram
is enabled by META_APP_ID and META_APP_SECRET
keeps working because Facebook Page tokens do not expire
cards.use: connect a Facebook Page or Instagram account
not: uses a Google OAuth client

cards.subject: Connect with Google
says: connects YouTube channels
refreshes Google tokens before they run out
needs the YouTube Data API v3 and the youtube.force-ssl and youtube.upload scopes
cards.use: connect a YouTube channel
not: uses a Meta app

cards.subject: An Instagram account for live mode
says: must be a business or creator account linked to a Facebook Page
needs the instagram_content_publish permission
cards.use: ask why an Instagram account cannot go live
not: can be a personal account

cards.subject: An unverified Google project
says: makes YouTube uploads private
lets only test users connect
cards.use: see uploaded videos come out private on YouTube
not: has no effect on uploads

cards.subject: A channel that needs reconnecting
says: is a channel the platform stopped accepting the sign-in for
drops back to manual so posts still go out through the publish queue
cards.use: see a live channel marked needs reconnecting
not: keeps trying to publish in live mode

cards.subject: Bluesky connection
says: uses an app password
reads replies and mentions into Engagement every ten minutes
reads back likes, replies and reposts but not reach
cards.use: connect a Bluesky account
not: uses an OAuth sign-in button

cards.subject: Mastodon connection
says: uses an application token from your instance
needs the read:notifications and read:statuses scopes as well as the posting ones
tells you in the channel when the platform refuses an older token
cards.use: see a Mastodon channel that posts but cannot read replies
not: needs only the posting scopes

cards.subject: The Google Photos import
says: opens Google's own picker in a new tab
imports only the photos and videos picked there
uses the photospicker.mediaitems.readonly scope
cards.use: ask why the app cannot browse a whole Photos library
not: browses the whole library inside the app

cards.subject: Live access for LinkedIn
says: needs the Community Management API with w_organization_social
has the slowest app review of the listed platforms
cards.use: need to tell the team which live platform review is slowest
not: needs no review

cards.subject: Live access for X
says: needs API Basic tier or above with OAuth 2.0 and tweet.write
needs no review but is paid
cards.use: need the live platform that is paid rather than reviewed
not: needs a long review but is free

cards.subject: Live access for Reddit
says: uses a script or web app from reddit.com/prefs/apps with the submit scope
needs no review
cards.use: need the live platform that uses reddit.com/prefs/apps
not: needs an audited app

cards.subject: Live access for Telegram
says: needs a bot from @BotFather
needs the bot added to the channel as admin
cards.use: need to publish to a Telegram channel
not: needs an app review

cards.subject: Live access for WhatsApp Business
says: needs a Meta app, business verification and approved templates
cards.use: need the live platform that requires business verification and approved templates
not: needs only a token

cards.subject: Next.js in GGSocial
says: is pinned exactly at 16.3.5 together with React 19.2.8
has breaking changes, so the bundled docs are checked first per AGENTS.md
cards.use: are about to change framework code and need the rule from AGENTS.md
not: can be assumed to behave like older Next.js

cards.subject: Drizzle and the postgres driver
says: are how GGSocial reads and writes Postgres
keep the schema in src/lib/db/schema.ts
cards.use: need the database library of the app
not: is Prisma with MySQL

cards.subject: drizzle-kit
says: pushes and generates the schema
is run by npm run db:push
is also used by the tests to push the real schema into PGlite
cards.use: need the tool that creates the tables
not: is the ORM used in queries

cards.subject: The GG UI kit
says: lives in src/gg-ui and is a copy of the kit shared with GGLeads
is stamped with its source commit in SOURCE.md
must not be edited in ggsocial
cards.use: want to change the sidebar or a stat tile
not: is edited directly in ggsocial

cards.subject: sync-ui.mjs
says: copies the GG UI kit from the GGLeads checkout
fails with --check if the copy was edited or is behind
cards.use: need to update or verify the UI kit copy
not: publishes the UI kit to npm

cards.subject: A platform adapter
says: is one file in src/lib/platforms/adapters
implements the Platform contract
needs one line in the registry
cards.use: need to add platform 110
not: is added by editing the composer component

cards.subject: The manualPlatform factory
says: builds a manual-only channel from a row in adapters/_catalog.ts
means channels with no write API skip the adapter file
cards.use: add a platform that has no write API
not: needs a full adapter file

cards.subject: Vitest in GGSocial
says: runs with npm test, which is vitest run
includes files matching tests/**/*.test.ts
uses a node environment with a 30-second timeout
cards.use: need to run the test suite
not: runs in a jsdom browser environment

cards.subject: PGlite in tests
says: is an in-memory Postgres built by tests/stubs/test-db.ts
lets database tests run without a running Postgres
has the real schema pushed into it through drizzle-kit's API
cards.use: need to test database code without Docker
not: connects to the production database

cards.subject: The deploy test gate
says: runs the type-check, lint and npm test before the deploy
stops the deploy when any of them fails
cards.use: ask what stops a broken change from being deployed
not: is run by the server after the build

cards.subject: Storing time in UTC
says: keeps one unambiguous instant for a post
is shown in each brand's timezone
cards.use: have brands in different timezones sharing one scheduler
not: stores the local clock time without a zone

cards.subject: Everyone logged out at once
says: is explained by APP_SECRET having changed
also leaves stored platform tokens undecryptable so channels need reconnecting
cards.use: get a report that all users and channels broke after a deploy
not: is explained by an expired Let's Encrypt certificate
like: A stale tab after a deploy

cards.subject: A stale tab after a deploy
says: fails with Failed to find Server Action
is prevented by the deploymentId, which makes Next reload the page
cards.use: get a report of an error on the first click after a deploy
not: means the user's role was removed

cards.subject: Readers seeing a 401 on a short link
says: means /l/ is behind the basic-auth wall
is fixed with a Require all granted Location block for /l/ in both vhosts
cards.use: are told strangers get a password prompt on tracked links
not: is fixed by changing the link's code

cards.subject: Instagram failing to fetch media
says: points to APP_URL not being reachable from the internet or the media route being behind the wall
is fixed by letting /api/media/file/ through
cards.use: get a report that an Instagram post fails at the media step
not: means the Instagram account is personal
like: Readers seeing a 401 on a short link

cards.subject: A viewer who cannot edit
says: is working as designed because the viewer role is read-only
is changed by an admin or owner giving a higher role
cards.use: get a ticket that a team member cannot edit a post
not: is a bug in the composer

cards.subject: An editor who cannot approve
says: is working as designed because approving needs the approver role or admin and above
is changed by giving the person approver or admin
cards.use: get a ticket that an editor cannot sign off a post
not: is a bug in the editor role

cards.subject: A post stuck in the publish queue
says: is waiting for a person to publish by hand on a manual channel
is cleared by ticking it off after posting
cards.use: get a ticket that a scheduled post on a manual-only platform has not gone out
not: means the scheduler crashed

cards.subject: A run paused for a person
says: lands in the Review inbox
is resolved by approving, sending back with a note or stopping the run
cards.use: get a ticket that an agent's reply never went out
not: is resolved by restarting pm2

cards.subject: A site down after a failed build
says: is checked first by polling /login
may mean the build failed after rm -rf .next with the wrong Node on the PATH
cards.use: see the site down right after a failed deploy
not: is fixed by rotating APP_SECRET

cards.subject: A content calendar
says: plans what is published, where and when
keeps several channels from posting at cross purposes
cards.use: need to plan posts across a month
not: replaces the need for any approval

cards.subject: A content pillar
says: is a recurring theme a brand posts about
keeps ideas on strategy
cards.use: need a theme to generate ideas around
not: is a single post

cards.subject: Brand voice
says: describes how the brand sounds in writing
should stay consistent across platforms
cards.use: write for a brand across several platforms
not: should change completely on every platform

cards.subject: Content repurposing
says: adapts one idea into several formats
respects each platform's format instead of copying text verbatim
cards.use: need to get more from one idea
not: means posting the same text everywhere unchanged

cards.subject: An approval gate
says: puts a second person between a draft and publishing
reduces the chance of an error or off-brand post going out
cards.use: want fewer mistakes in published content
not: is unnecessary when the writer is senior

cards.subject: Community moderation
says: reviews and responds to comments and messages
removes or escalates abusive content
sends sensitive matters to a person
cards.use: need to handle a hostile comment on a brand post
not: leaves every comment to an automatic reply

cards.subject: An escalation path
says: says who must decide when a matter is sensitive
covers prices, refunds, legal and health matters in this app's safety stops
cards.use: face a complaint that mentions a refund or legal threat
not: lets any editor reply immediately

cards.subject: UTM parameters
says: tag a link so analytics can attribute the visit
identify source, medium and campaign
cards.use: need to know which post a visit came from
not: change how the link looks on the platform

cards.subject: A posting window
says: is a time range when a brand's audience is likely to be active
can be suggested from what performed in the past
cards.use: choose when to schedule a post
not: is fixed for all brands and platforms

cards.subject: Reach
says: counts the unique accounts that saw a post
is not reported by Bluesky or Mastodon in this app
cards.use: need how many different people saw a post
not: counts every time a post was shown, repeats included

cards.subject: Impressions
says: count every time a post was shown
can exceed reach because one person may see a post more than once
cards.use: need total displays of a post
not: count unique accounts

cards.subject: Engagement rate
says: divides interactions such as likes, comments and shares by an audience measure
compares posts of different audience sizes
cards.use: compare a small account's post with a large one
not: is the number of followers

cards.subject: Click-through rate
says: divides clicks by the number of times a link was shown
measures how well a post drives traffic
cards.use: judge how well a link in a post attracts clicks
not: divides likes by followers

cards.subject: Follower growth
says: is the net change in followers over a period
is read daily by the goals job in this app
cards.use: track how an audience changes over time
not: counts the people who saw one post

cards.subject: Response time
says: is how long a brand takes to answer a comment or message
is a service measure of community management
cards.use: judge how quickly the team replies to people
not: is how fast the page loads

qa.q: In GGSocial, what is a brand?
qa.right: One company or project with its own channels, media, calendar, team and timezone
wrong: A single account on a single platform
qa.why: The README defines a brand as one company or project.

qa.q: How many platforms does GGSocial cover in 11 categories?
qa.why: 109 platforms: 45 live, 64 manual-only.

qa.q: A platform has no write API for organic content. What does GGSocial do?
qa.right: Composes, validates, schedules and queues the post for a person to publish with copy-ready blocks
wrong: Emails the post to the brand owner
qa.why: Manual channels get the same flow and end with a person clicking publish.

qa.q: Which role is read-only?
qa.right: Viewer
qa.why: The viewer role is read-only.

qa.q: Which database and ORM does GGSocial use?
qa.right: Postgres with Drizzle
qa.why: The schema is in src/lib/db/schema.ts.

qa.q: A user must write a Reddit post in the composer. What must it have?
qa.right: A title and a subreddit
qa.why: Reddit needs a title and a subreddit.

qa.q: A team wants a person to sign off posts but not change them. Which role?
qa.right: Approver
qa.why: Approver is review only and cannot edit.

qa.q: Where does a post for a manual channel appear when it is due?
qa.right: In the publish queue with copy buttons, media and steps
wrong: In the Review inbox as a safety stop
Nowhere until the scheduler publishes it
qa.why: Ticking it off marks it published.

qa.q: Which agent reads yesterday's posts each morning?
qa.right: The performance analyst
qa.why: It also writes weekly and monthly reports.

qa.q: How are passwords stored?
qa.right: Hashed with bcrypt at cost 12
qa.why: bcryptjs at cost 12.

qa.q: What is the session cookie called, and what does it hold?
qa.right: ggs_session, a signed JWT
qa.why: HS256 via jose, httpOnly, SameSite lax, 30 days.

qa.q: What is the lowest role that may edit and publish?
qa.right: Editor
qa.why: Editing and publishing need editor or above.

qa.q: An owner turns off review for the community manager's reply step. A draft reply mentions a refund. What happens?
qa.right: The run still pauses, because a flagged risk is a safety stop whatever the setting
wrong: It publishes because review is off
It is sent to the viewer role
qa.why: Safety stops override the review setting.

qa.q: Which of these is a post status but NOT a target status?
qa.right: changes_requested
qa.why: Targets have pending, scheduled, publishing, awaiting_manual, published, failed and skipped.

qa.q: Your team needs the app to stop searching outside signals when the strategist plans ideas. What do you set?
qa.right: RESEARCH_SIGNALS=off
qa.why: By default it searches Hacker News for the last 30 days.

qa.q: The scheduler is not running in development. Scheduled posts never go out. What command do you run in a second terminal?
qa.right: npm run scheduler
qa.why: Scheduled posts are dispatched by a scheduler tick, not the web request.

qa.q: A new setup needs uploads that survive on Vercel. Which setting?
qa.right: MEDIA_DRIVER=s3
qa.why: Serverless filesystems are wiped between invocations.

qa.q: Which header carries the agent API token?
qa.right: X-Agent-Token
qa.why: Basic auth already occupies the Authorization header.

qa.q: Why does a server action re-check the role even though the UI hides the button?
qa.right: Hiding a button is not the security boundary
qa.why: The check is on the server.

qa.q: An editor on Brand A calls the add-team-member action directly. What happens?
qa.right: It is refused because managing the team needs admin or above
wrong: It succeeds because editors can write
qa.why: requireBrandRole throws when the role is too low.

qa.q: A user says an editor cannot approve their own post. What is the correct reading of the code?
qa.right: Approving needs approver or admin and above, so an editor cannot approve
wrong: Any role at or above editor can approve
qa.why: Editor is not in the approval rule.

qa.q: Which of these is NOT a safety stop?
qa.right: The post uses an emoji
wrong: The daily AI budget is spent
qa.why: Emojis are not a safety stop.

qa.q: What does the reviewer do with weak but safe work?
qa.right: Sends it back to the agent once with fixes before asking a person
qa.why: Only then is a person asked.

qa.q: What does a changed APP_SECRET do?
qa.right: Logs everyone out and makes stored platform tokens undecryptable
qa.why: Channels would need reconnecting.

qa.q: Why must APP_URL be reachable from the internet in production?
qa.right: Platform APIs fetch media from it
qa.why: Instagram, Facebook, Pinterest and TikTok fetch media with no credentials.

qa.q: How do you add a manual-only platform with no write API?
qa.right: Add a row to adapters/_catalog.ts and let manualPlatform() build the rest
wrong: Write a full adapter and registry line
qa.why: Platforms with a write API need an adapter file plus one registry line.

qa.q: What does a normal npm run deploy do on your machine before it syncs?
qa.right: Type-checks, lints and runs the tests; a failure in any stops the deploy
qa.why: SKIP_TESTS=1 skips all three, for an emergency only.

qa.q: How do database tests run without Docker?
qa.right: An in-memory PGlite database with the real schema pushed in
wrong: They connect to the production database
They mock every query by hand
qa.why: tests/stubs/test-db.ts builds it.

qa.q: A Mastodon channel posts fine but replies never arrive in Engagement. Most likely cause?
qa.right: The token lacks the read:notifications and read:statuses scopes
qa.why: Older tokens must be created again with the scopes.

qa.q: Which pm2 process ticks /api/cron/publish?
qa.right: ggsocial-scheduler, every 60 seconds
qa.why: It also calls the agents endpoint every 5 minutes.

qa.q: A deploy shows one `tick failed: fetch failed` in the scheduler log. What does it mean?
qa.right: It is expected during the restart window; repeated ones are not
qa.why: The scheduler fetches while the web process restarts.

qa.q: A user reports Failed to find Server Action after your deploy. What is the cause?
qa.right: A tab left open on the old build calls an id the new build lacks
qa.why: deploymentId makes Next reload when ids differ.

qa.q: After a failed build, a retry replays the same error. What avoids it?
qa.right: Build into a fresh .next-new each time
qa.why: Turbopack caches the failure.

qa.q: The deploy script ran rsync with --delete and the site lost all logins. What was missing?
qa.right: --exclude .env
qa.why: .env is not in the repo, so rsync deletes it.

qa.q: Editing sites-available/ggsocial.gglink.co.uk-le-ssl.conf passed configtest and reloaded but changed nothing. Why?
qa.right: The live :443 vhost is a regular file in sites-enabled, not a symlink
qa.why: Check with apachectl -S.

qa.q: The build fails with Node.js version >=20.9.0 is required. What is the usual cause in this deploy?
qa.right: bash -lc sources nvm and puts Node 18 first
qa.why: Put /usr/bin first on the PATH.

qa.q: The build dies with Cannot find module './tailwindcss-oxide.linux-x64-gnu.node'. What do you do?
qa.right: Install @tailwindcss/oxide-linux-x64-gnu with --no-save at the installed oxide version
wrong: Run next dev on the server
qa.why: The macOS lockfile omits the optional dependency.

qa.q: A drizzle-kit push stops with a prompt. Why not use --force?
qa.right: It would auto-approve a drop if the live schema drifted
qa.why: Run with < /dev/null so it fails fast.

qa.q: Which of these keeps the old build serving while the new one builds?
qa.right: Building into .next-new and swapping it in
qa.why: Only the restart is a gap.

qa.q: The agent API is behind the basic-auth wall. What is the correct fix?
qa.right: Add a Require all granted Location /api/agent/ block, since each route rejects bad tokens itself
qa.why: Both vhosts need it.

qa.q: A community manager's reply is about a legal threat. What happens even if review is off?
qa.right: It pauses in the Review inbox as a flagged risk
wrong: It is posted as a draft
qa.why: Legal matters are flagged risks.

qa.q: A post to YouTube has the title but the upload shows private. What is the likely reason?
qa.right: The Google project is not yet verified
qa.why: Until verification, uploads are private and only test users connect.

qa.q: Your Instagram post fails at the media step in production. What do you check first?
qa.right: APP_URL reachable from the internet and /api/media/file/ let past the wall
qa.why: Instagram fetches media from APP_URL without credentials.

qa.q: A user wants to know which table gives them a role per brand.
qa.right: memberships
qa.why: One row per user and brand with a unique index.

qa.q: A scheduled post to Medium has not gone out. Where is it?
qa.right: In the publish queue, waiting for a person to post it
qa.why: Medium is manual-only.

qa.q: What does Bluesky use to connect?
qa.right: An app password
qa.why: Mastodon uses an application token.

qa.q: A reader sees a 401 on a /l/ short link. What is the fix?
qa.right: Add a Require all granted Location /l/ to both vhosts and reload Apache
qa.why: Short links must pass the basic-auth wall.

qa.q: A brand owner wants agents to stop pausing for review on one step. What is required?
qa.right: The owner switches that step's review off with a reason that is kept in the log
wrong: A super admin edits the database
Nothing; review is off by default
qa.why: Review is on for every step until the owner switches it off.

qa.q: A brand wants a social post to read well across platforms. What is a good practice?
qa.right: Adapt the idea to each platform's format instead of pasting the same text
qa.why: Repurposing respects each platform.

qa.q: A client asks how many unique people saw a post. Which metric?
qa.right: Reach
qa.why: Impressions count repeats.

qa.q: A comment from an angry customer arrives. What is the right handling?
qa.right: Draft a reply but route it to a person to decide if it is a sensitive matter
qa.why: Complaints and apologies are flagged risks here.

qa.q: A support ticket says an approver 'can't fix a typo'. What do you tell them?
qa.right: The approver role is review only; send the post back with a change request so an editor fixes it
wrong: Give the approver the owner role
qa.why: Separation of duties.

qa.q: An admin asks what to do after changing the schema in code. Which order is right at deploy?
qa.right: Push the schema before restarting, or the new build will query columns that do not exist
qa.why: drizzle-kit push comes before the restart.

qa.q: Someone wants to edit src/gg-ui/ in ggsocial to change a badge. What do you advise?
qa.right: Change it in GGLeads (packages/ui) and copy it across with node scripts/sync-ui.mjs
qa.why: A --check run fails if the copy was edited.
